title: Emergence Theory

hero.headline: Persistence becomes generative when a grammar can preserve and promote it.
hero.support: A recovered landing projection for the research program studying how stable distinctions, boundaries, invariants, defects, and admissible compositions become higher-level structure.

sections.heading: From persistence to structure
sections.body: Emergence is treated as more than aggregation: persistent lower-level structure can become a lawful primitive at a higher level when its relevant invariants survive promotion.

sections.heading: Contexture matters
sections.body: What can emerge depends on the declared environment, available distinctions, admissible operations, boundaries, and closure conditions.

sections.heading: Defect is informative
sections.body: Failure to close exposes the residue or obstruction that a higher-level description must account for.

sections.heading: Micro to macro
sections.body: The research program studies projection, lift, boundary transport, invariant preservation, and promotion as a concrete bridge between levels of description.

sections.heading: Current theoretical position
sections.body: Emergence Theory is now a major facet of Boundary Theory rather than the umbrella name for the entire research corpus.

notes: Recovered from the earlier eight-page landing-page set.
